allies.rationale_text: Growth-mindset gives persistence-grit the belief that hard effort can actually build capacity over time.
allies.source_quote: behavioral expression of the Growth Mindset
allies.affinity_rationale: Canonical: 'Grit is a behavioral expression of the Growth Mindset, which believes intelligence and character are dynamic and can be developed' — intrinsic relationship.
allies.activation_condition: When sustained effort requires the belief that abilities can develop through dedication and hard work.

allies.rationale_text: Deliberate-practice gives persistence-grit a structured way to turn endurance into improvement rather than mere repetition.
allies.affinity_rationale: Canonical: Deep Work (close cousin of deliberate practice) 'requires the ability to concentrate without distraction'; grit provides the stamina for persistent engagement.
allies.activation_condition: When persistence must be directed through structured, focused practice to build genuine expertise.

antagonists.rationale_text: Einstellung-effect undermines persistence-grit by channeling sustained effort into a familiar but inappropriate framework, turning grit into stubborn repetition of the wrong approach.
antagonists.source_quote: Persistence can lead to the inappropriate application of familiar mental models to genuinely novel problems. This is the trap of Maslow's hammer: If the only tool you have is a hammer, to treat everything as if it were a nail. This results in persisting with frameworks that are unhelpful or misleading.
antagonists.affinity_rationale: Canonical risks: 'Inertia / Doubling Down — refusing to quit a failing course of action' due to rigid persistence in familiar approaches.
antagonists.activation_condition: When rigid persistence in a familiar approach prevents adoption of more effective strategies.

antagonists.rationale_text: Status-quo-bias undermines persistence-grit by converting purposeful endurance into inertia, causing people and organizations to double down on existing courses of action driven by the momentum of previous commitment rather than evidence.
antagonists.source_quote: Inertia Default: This bias causes people and organizations to double down on existing courses of action, even when they are fundamentally wrong, driven by the sheer momentum of previous commitment.
antagonists.affinity_rationale: Canonical risks: persistence can anchor to current course; 'Ambiguity Aversion' leads to forcing conclusions rather than adapting.
antagonists.activation_condition: When persistence anchors to the current course rather than adapting to changing conditions or evidence.

structured_tensions.tension_text: Persistence-grit conflicts with sunk-cost-fallacy when continued effort becomes escalation despite failing evidence.
Persistence-grit conflicts with commitment-bias when identity-level resolve blocks a needed strategic pivot.
Persistence-grit conflicts with confirmation-bias when people selectively notice evidence that continued effort is working.

curation_notes.summary: Layer 1+2 enrichment complete. growth-mindset at 0.90 ('behavioral expression of'), deliberate-practice at 0.80. Both antagonists at 0.80. Canonical structured tensions also flag sunk-cost-fallacy and commitment-bias as conflicts.
open_questions: SPARSE_ALLY_RECOVERY: 2 curated allies. Canonical mentions commitment-and-consistency (psychological reinforcement loop) and hypothesis-driven-problem-solving (iterative testing requires grit).
